description: Course item E (settled 2026-08-20). (1) THE FLATTENING IS A DELETION: nothing writes layout/logs/ except the recovery transaction, and FDB confirms the doctrine - TLog membership is generation-constant; changing log topology IS a recovery (new epoch, new logSystemConfig). RoutingData's second way of managing the log table (insert_log arrival-order append, remove_log reindex, delete_log_service, clear_logs_in_range in the mutation fold) guards a structurally-precluded hazard: the only layout_log mutations that ever flow through a window are the recovery transaction's rewrite of the set the proxy was just seeded with. Delete the fold handling; log wiring is seed-only and epoch-constant; topology remains the single once-per-epoch builder. The layout/logs/ FAMILY STAYS (user decision 2026-08-20): recovery keeps writing it for other consumers and cluster introspection tools - update the SystemKeys/persistence 'named reader' comments to say so rather than implying a code reader. (2) shard_layout_from_entries (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:505-537) DISCARDS the start_key that Values.decode_shard_key_entry returns and rebuilds it from sorted end-key adjacency while RoutingData.apply_mutation consumes it correctly - two readers of one family disagreeing about what the value means. Consume the decoded start_key; adjacency survives only inside the legacy fallback (dies with q67.20.7). (3) materializer_refs (transaction_system_layout.ex:55-69) linear-scans services to recover worker_ids the bootstrap had in hand at creation (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:131-141) - carry {tag -> {worker_id, node, pid}} on the attempt and delete the inversion. Low-priority noted: ResolverLayout.calculate_resolver_ends adjacency rebuild (recovery-internal, single reader).
title: Log wiring is epoch-constant: delete RoutingData's mid-epoch log handling; kill re-derivations
